title: Agent state per pane lives apart from the router's client claims
body:
`Workspace.agents: HashMap<String, Agent { state, message, client }>` is keyed by pane name and stores the client id, while `Router` already knows which client holds which pane. Cleanup is written three times: by client id on disconnect (`retain(.. agent.client != id)`), and by pane name at both pane-removal sites. `Host::Status` carries `client` and `pane` only so the compositor can rebuild that link.

Separately, `Router::connected` inserts a `Client { name: None, .. }` before hello, and `hello` repeats the literal through `entry().or_insert`. The "say hello first" check tests `name`, and reads end in `unwrap_or_default()` and `unwrap_or("another client")`.

## Proposal

`status: Option<(AgentState, Option<String>)>` on `channel::Client`, so disconnect and pane removal clear it with the claim, and `Workspace::agent_state` takes the max over the router's clients. Insert a client only at `hello`, with `name: String`; "hello first" becomes `!clients.contains_key(&id)`.
